sanskrit_verse: अन्धो मत्स्यान् इवाश्नाति निरपेक्षः सकण्टकान् । परोक्षम् अर्थवैकल्याद् भाषते यः सभां गतः ॥
transliteration: andho matsyān ivāśnāti nirapekṣaḥ sakaṇṭakān | parokṣam arthavaikalyād bhāṣate yaḥ sabhāṃ gataḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who, having entered the assembly, speaks indirectly due to deficiency in clarity or intent, is like a blind man consuming fish with bones—heedless and causing harm through unawareness.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from clarity of expression and conscious intent
Causation is determined by awareness and capacity to convey truth
Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment of speech with inner realization
Restoration logic demands correction of misaligned communication
Consciousness alignment is prerequisite for lawful utterance in sacred assemblies
executable_legal_axioms: IF speaker lacks clarity in expression AND causes misunderstanding THEN initiate completion process for communicative alignment
IF speech originates without sankalpa (intentional will) THEN assign responsibility for re-expression under supervision
IF indirect speech leads to distortion of dharma THEN mandate pramana-based restatement within 24 hours
IF speaker demonstrates habitual deficiency THEN enroll in sankalpa-vak restoration protocol
supreme_court_application: In the highest judicial forum, any indirect or ambiguous statement that distorts dharma must be immediately rectified. The court shall assess the speaker's capacity and intent; if found deficient, restoration protocols supersede procedural continuation until clarity is restored.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality establishes that unclear speech disrupts dharma transmission. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how defective expression leads to collective misalignment. Responsibility is proportional to one’s capacity for clarity. Non-punitive rule ensures correction without condemnation, aligning the speaker with satya-vak.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate vak-shuddhi (speech purification) process involving guided repetition of truthful articulation
Assign mentorship under realized speaker for minimum three sabha sessions
Require written clarification within prescribed time followed by oral reaffirmation
Enroll in sankalpa-sthiti training to restore integrity between thought, word, and action
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Speech in dharma-sabha must arise from awakened consciousness. Deficiency is not condemned but corrected. Dharma is restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone is the Supreme Adjudicator.
